subtitle: How a Kashmiri Saint Turned Labor and Restraint into a Valley’s Quiet Law

panels.shot: wide, misty valley vista with low-angle focus on Nund Rishi seated under a tall chinar, mountains looming behind
panels.action: Nund Rishi sits cross-legged beneath a great chinar tree, simple and calm, the Kashmir Valley stretching away in mist and terrace fields, snow peaks watching from the horizon.

dialogue.text: In a Kashmir of temples, shrines and rival claims, Nund Rishi spoke in Kashmiri of labor, restraint and mercy—and his quiet ethic outlived the arguments over who owned the valley’s soul.

i18n.hi: मंदिरों, ज़ियारतों और टकरावों के कश्मीर में नुंद ऋषि ने मेहनत, संयम और रहम की बात कश्मीरी में की — और उनकी शांत नीति ने घाटी की रूह पर चले सारे झगड़े पीछे छोड़ दिए।

panels.shot: slow push-in from high valley view towards a modest village near Kulgam
panels.action: Terraced fields, wooden houses and a winding stream near Kulgam lie under a pale sky; in the distance a young shepherd boy, later Nund Rishi, walks with a flock along the slope.

dialogue.text: Late fourteenth-century Kashmir was a valley between worlds—old Shaiva and Buddhist lineages, new sultans and Sufis, villagers watching from their fields and hearths.

i18n.hi: चौदहवीं सदी के आख़िर का कश्मीर दुनिया के बीच की घाटी था — पुराने शैव और बौद्ध वंश, नए सुल्तान और सूफी, खेत-खलिहान से सब देखते गाँव वाले।

panels.shot: medium shot of the young Nund Rishi in a village lane, half in shadow, half in light
panels.action: A teenage Nund Rishi, lean and simple in homespun wool, pauses in a narrow village lane, eyes distant, while men argue near a shrine and a mosque beyond.

dialogue.text: Out of Kulgam’s earth came Noor-ud-Din, later called Nund Rishi—a village boy watching sharp tongues and soft hearts share the same streets.

i18n.hi: कुलगाम की मिट्टी से उठा नूरुद्दीन, आगे चलकर नुंद ऋषि — गाँव का लड़का, जो एक ही गली में तीखी ज़ुबानें और नरम दिलों को चलते देखता था।

panels.shot: interior wide of a simple wooden room where elders debate, Nund Rishi listens at the edge
panels.action: In a dim wooden room lit by a small oil lamp, elders in varied dress talk with tense faces of new Muslim rulers and old temple lands, while young Nund Rishi listens quietly at the edge.

dialogue.text: New Muslim sultans ruled from Srinagar, land grants shifted, shrines jostled for favor. Villagers weighed fear and hope, and the words for God changed on official tongues.

i18n.hi: सिरिनगर से नए मुस्लिम सुल्तान हुकूमत करते, ज़मीनें बदलतीं, मज़ारें मेहरबानी के लिए टकरातीं। गाँव वाले डर और उम्मीद तौलते, और हुक्मरानों की ज़ुबान पर खुदा के नाम बदलते जाते।

panels.shot: soft wide shot by a riverbank with Lal Ded as a distant, anonymous figure; Nund Rishi watches in awe
panels.action: By a river, an older woman ascetic moves along the stones reciting verses, while Nund Rishi watches from across the water, the wind carrying her words through poplar trees.

dialogue.text: Tradition remembers him hearing Lal Ded’s Kashmiri verses on the road and riverbank—an older voice tearing at empty ritual, praising inner truth in the valley’s own tongue.

i18n.hi: रिवायत है कि उसने राहों और नदी किनारे पर लाल देद के कश्मीरी शेर सुने — पुरानी आवाज़, सूने कर्मकांड को चीरती, भीतर की सच्चाई को घाटी की अपनी भाषा में सराहती।

panels.shot: close-up on Nund Rishi’s face as he hears verses, eyes reflecting water and firelight
panels.action: Nund Rishi’s face fills the frame, eyes wide and wet, the river glittering behind; his lips move silently as he repeats a Kashmiri line he has just heard.

dialogue.text: Her shivras spoke of the divine beyond label, mocked hypocrisy. For a young Noor-ud-Din, they showed that the valley’s everyday speech could carry the weight of awakening.

i18n.hi: उसके शिवर ने नाम से परे ईश्वरीय को गुनगुनाया, ढोंग पर तंज कसा। कमसिन नूरुद्दीन के लिए ये सबक थे कि घाटी की रोज़ की बोली भी जागरण का बोझ उठा सकती है।

panels.shot: wide shot of a hillside cave or hut where Nund Rishi sits alone in meditation
panels.action: On a lonely hillside above fields and orchards, Nund Rishi sits in a small stone shelter, wrapped in a rough shawl, eyes closed in stillness as evening smoke rises from the valley below.

dialogue.text: He turned inward, took the path of a Muslim faqir, but not of imported Persian orders. In his solitude the shape of an indigenous Kashmiri Rishi way began to form.

i18n.hi: वो भीतर मुड़ा, मुसलमान फ़क़ीर की राह ली, मगर बाहर से आई फ़ारसी सिलसिलों से अलग। उसकी तन्हाई में एक देसी कश्मीरी ‘ऋषि’ राह का नक्शा बनने लगा।

panels.shot: medium shot in a simple orchard where Nund Rishi works with his hands, villagers watch
panels.action: In a modest orchard near a village, Nund Rishi stands with villagers, sleeves rolled, planting saplings and tilling soil, his face calm, while others look on with a mix of respect and surprise.

dialogue.text: He refused luxury, worked the earth with his own hands. His path made labor itself a devotion—and shamed holy men who lived off gifts while preaching renunciation.

i18n.hi: उसने ऐश ठुकराई, अपने हाथों से ज़मीन जोती। उसकी राह में मेहनत ही इबादत बनी — और उन मौलानाओं को आईना दिखाया जो तज्रिद का ख़ुत्बा देकर नज़राने पर जीते थे।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of a hut with Nund Rishi dictating shruks to a disciple by lamplight
panels.action: Inside a low wooden hut, lit by a small lamp, Nund Rishi sits on a mat, speaking measured words in Kashmiri as a disciple listens and traces lines on a palm-leaf or paper.

dialogue.text: His shruks—short Kashmiri verses—poured out of this hut and field, praising restraint, mercy and simple living. In them, the valley’s speech became a language of Sufi reflection.

i18n.hi: उसकी श्रुक — छोटे कश्मीरी शेर — इसी झोंपड़ी और खेत से निकले, संयम, रहम और सादा ज़िंदगी की तरफ़ बुलाते। उनमें घाटी की बोली सूफी सोच की ज़बान बन गई।

panels.shot: close-up of Nund Rishi’s hand scattering grain to birds outside, disciples watch
panels.action: Nund Rishi kneels by a threshold, scattering grain for birds, a gentle smile on his face, while two younger men behind him watch, moved by the small act.

dialogue.text: Khwaja Azam Diddamari later wrote of his tenderness—feeding birds, refusing violence. The Rishi ethic held that harming creatures darkened the heart and the valley together.

i18n.hi: ख़्वाजा अज़म दिद्दामारी ने बाद में उसकी नर्मी लिखी — पंछियों को खिलाना, हिंसा से इन्कार। ऋषि नीति मानती थी कि ज़ातों को दुख देने से दिल भी और घाटी भी एक साथ मैली होती है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Nund Rishi speaking to a mixed group near Charar-e-Sharif, shrine and village in background
panels.action: Near Charar-e-Sharif, Nund Rishi stands on a gentle slope, speaking calmly to men and women from different communities, with a simple shrine and village houses behind them.

dialogue.text: “If you till, eat, and share with restraint, the quarrel over names loses its sting.”

i18n.hi: "जोत, खा और बाँट — मगर संयम के साथ, तो नामों का झगड़ा काट नहीं सकेगा।"

panels.shot: wide crowd shot, some in Hindu dress, some in Muslim, listening under tall trees
panels.action: Under tall trees, a mixed gathering sits in a wide semicircle around Nund Rishi, their clothes showing different traditions, their faces united in intent listening.

dialogue.text: His circle drew Hindus and Muslims. He did not erase difference; he planted a shared ethic—honest work, self-restraint, compassion—as the ground they could stand on together.

i18n.hi: उसके घेरे में हिंदू भी आए, मुसलमान भी। उसने फ़र्क़ नहीं मिटाया; उसने साझा नीति बोई — सच्ची मेहनत, आत्म-संयम, करुणा — ताकि सब उसी ज़मीन पर साथ खड़े हो सकें।

panels.shot: documentary-style montage wide: Sufi khanqah, temple, and Rishi hut all in one valley frame
panels.action: A broad valley shot frames a temple spire, a Sufi khanqah, and Nund Rishi’s modest hut in different corners, smoke rising from homes between them, mountains holding the scene.

dialogue.text: Modern historians see the Rishi order as one stream in Kashmir’s gradual Islamization—alongside court politics, land disputes, and other Sufi networks, not as the single tide that turned the valley.

i18n.hi: आज के इतिहासकार ऋषि सिलसिले को कश्मीर की नर्म इस्लामीकरण की एक धारा मानते हैं — दरबार की सियासत, ज़मीन की खींचतान और दूसरे सूफी जालों के साथ, न कि अकेली लहर जिसने घाटी बदल दी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Nund Rishi gently declining rich gifts from a courtier, villagers watch
panels.action: A finely dressed courtier offers folded cloth and coins to Nund Rishi, who raises a hand and smiles, refusing, while villagers nearby watch with quiet approval.

dialogue.text: Stories in Rishi Namah remember him turning away from sultans’ favors, wary of courts that mixed piety with power and used religion to sanctify new hierarchies.

i18n.hi: रिशि नामह की कहानियाँ याद रखती हैं कि उसने सुल्तानों की मेहरबानियाँ ठुकराईं — उन दरबारों से बचते हुए जो दीन को ताक़त से मिलाकर नए दर्जे पवित्र घोषित करते थे।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Nund Rishi under a tree, quoting Lal Ded, mountains behind
panels.action: Nund Rishi stands beneath a tree, hand raised slightly, as if recalling a verse; the mountains behind him seem to lean closer, the sky clear and cold.

dialogue.text: He praised Lal Ded’s wisdom in his shruks, naming a woman saint from an older Shaiva world as a teacher. In that gesture, he stitched traditions without erasing their edges.

i18n.hi: उसने अपनी श्रुक में लाल देद की दानिश की तारीफ़ की, पुराने शैव संसार की एक औरत संत को उस्ताद कहा। इस इशारे से उसने परंपराएँ जोड़ीं, बिना उनकी सरहदें मिटाए।

panels.shot: interior hut shot with Nund Rishi frail in final days, disciples around in silence
panels.action: Inside a dim hut, an aging Nund Rishi lies with a calm, tired face, disciples seated around him in quiet vigil, a small lamp flickering beside woven blankets.

dialogue.text: He died around 1438, in a Kashmir still full of tension and difference. His passing did not end conflict—but it left an order whose measure of holiness was humility and service.

i18n.hi: लगभग १४३८ के आस-पास वो चला गया, एक ऐसे कश्मीर में जो अब भी खिंचाव और फ़र्क़ों से भरा था। उसके जाने से टकराव ख़त्म नहीं हुए — मगर पीछे एक ऐसा सिलसिला रह गया जिसमें पाकी की कसौटी विनम्रता और सेवा थी।

panels.shot: wide shot of Charar-e-Sharif shrine through time: subtle visual cues of changing architecture and pilgrims
panels.action: Charar-e-Sharif stands on its hill, wooden architecture changed across centuries hinted in layered outlines, pilgrims moving in quiet lines as clouds drift over the surrounding valley.

dialogue.text: Charar-e-Sharif became the heart of the Rishi memory, rebuilt and revisited across centuries—its wooden beams holding stories of famine, fire, and still, people gathering for Nund Rishi’s verses.

i18n.hi: चरार-ए-शरीफ़ ऋषि याद का दिल बना, सदियों से बार-बार बनता और सजता रहा — उसकी लकड़ी की बलियाँ अकाल, आग और फिर भी, नुंद ऋषि के शेर सुनने जुटते लोगों की कहानियाँ सँभाले हैं।

panels.shot: close-up of an old Kashmiri manuscript of shruks, pages gently turned by unseen hands
panels.action: An aged Kashmiri manuscript lies open on a woven mat; an unseen hand turns the page, revealing lines in flowing script, as light from a small window falls across the paper.

dialogue.text: Without an autograph, his shruks live in oral chains, manuscripts, and memory. Through them, Kashmiri itself survived as a language that could speak of God, ethics and doubt.

i18n.hi: उसके पास अपनी लिखावट नहीं, उसके श्रुक ज़बानी सिलसिलों, किताबों और यादों में बचे हैं। इन्हीं से कश्मीरी ज़बान बची रही — खुदा, नैतिकता और शक तक की बात कहने वाली भाषा के रूप में।

panels.shot: final sweeping wide of Kashmir valley at dawn, faint overlay of Nund Rishi’s figure seated under a chinar
panels.action: At dawn the Kashmir Valley glows in soft light—terraces, river, shrines, and homes; under a chinar, a faint, almost ghostly Nund Rishi sits, watching in silence.

dialogue.text: In a land still marked by contesting labels, Nund Rishi endures as a reminder that a shared ethic—work, restraint, mercy—can be the valley’s true shrine, if people choose to inhabit it.

i18n.hi: उपाधियों की खींचतान से आज भी चिह्नित इस ज़मीन में नुंद ऋषि इस बात की याद बनकर रहता है कि साझा नीति — मेहनत, संयम, रहम — ही घाटी की सच्ची ज़ियारत बन सकती है, अगर लोग उसे अपना घर बनाएँ।

title_i18n.hi: नुंद ऋषि ने कश्मीर की नीति बोई

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Kashmiri Saint Turned Labor and Restraint into a Valley’s Quiet Law
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे एक कश्मीरी सूफी ने मेहनत और संयम को घाटी का मौन कानून बना दिया
